## 2. One-Time Migration Cost

### 2.1 Team Delivery Cost

The programme requires 6–7 people across ~28 weeks (7 months). The following uses blended day rates indicative of a UK public-sector Cognizant engagement:

| Role | FTE Allocation | Duration (weeks) | Blended Day Rate | Estimated Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Executive Sponsor | 5% (oversight only) | 28 | £1,200/day | £8,400 |
| Delivery Lead / PM | 100% | 28 | £850/day | £119,000 |
| Cloud / Solutions Architect | 75% | 28 | £950/day | £99,750 |
| Senior Developer 1 (VB.NET) | 100% | 22 (Phases 1–5) | £800/day | £88,000 |
| Senior Developer 2 (.NET 10) | 100% | 24 (Phases 1–6) | £800/day | £96,000 |
| QA Engineer | 75% | 20 (Phases 0, 3, 5, 6) | £650/day | £65,000 |
| DevOps Engineer | 50% | 6 (Phases 1 + 6) | £750/day | £22,500 |

**Subtotal (people):** £498,650 — indicative midpoint of £410,000–£530,000 range  
*(Lower bound assumes AI productivity uplift of 30–35%; upper bound assumes no AI uplift)*

### 2.2 GitHub Copilot Tooling

7 users × £19/user/month × 18 months = **£2,394** (~£2,400)

### 2.3 Azure Infrastructure (Provisioning Effort)

Bicep templates generated by `azure-infra-implementer.agent` reduce provisioning effort to approximately **4 days DevOps + 2 days Architect review** for all four environments (dev, test, UAT, prod) = ~£5,600–£7,600.

## 3. AI Productivity Uplift Assumptions

GitHub Copilot augmentation applies directly to mechanical conversion tasks that form the majority of the migration workload:

| Task | Without AI (est. days) | With AI (est. days) | Uplift |
|---|---|---|---|
| VB.NET → C# translation of 185 source files | 120 days | 70 days | 42% |
| Bicep infrastructure modules (4 environments) | 15 days | 9 days | 40% |
| xUnit test generation for domain logic (70+ tests) | 10 days | 3 days | 70% |
| Crystal Reports → Playwright PDF (9 reports) | 25 days | 14 days | 44% |
| Razor Pages scaffold (64 pages) | 80 days | 50 days | 38% |
| CI/CD pipeline authoring | 8 days | 4 days | 50% |
| **Total mechanical effort** | **258 days** | **150 days** | **42% average uplift** |

**Net team saving from AI augmentation:** ~108 developer-days × £800/day = **£86,400 saved** relative to a non-AI-augmented equivalent programme.

This saving is already embedded in the team cost estimate above (the lower bound of the range assumes AI uplift is realised in full).

## 4. Ongoing Operational Cost (Post-Migration)

### 4.1 Azure Infrastructure — Annual Estimate

The target architecture runs as a single containerised application on Azure App Service. The following uses Azure UK South pricing (July 2026 indicative rates):

| Resource | Tier | Annual Cost (est.) |
|---|---|---|
| App Service Plan (P1v3, 1 instance) | Premium v3 | £4,800/year |
| Azure SQL Database (General Purpose, 2 vCores, 5 GB) | GP_Gen5_2 | £3,200/year |
| Azure Cache for Redis (C1 Standard) | Standard | £1,800/year |
| Azure Key Vault (Standard, ~20 secrets) | Standard | £120/year |
| Application Insights (first 5 GB free, est. 2 GB/month) | Pay-as-you-go | £600/year |
| Azure Container Registry (Basic) | Basic | £120/year |
| Storage Account (Blob for exports, LRS) | LRS Hot | £240/year |
| **Total Azure annual cost (prod environment only)** | | **£10,880/year** |
| Dev + Test + UAT environments (50% of prod cost) | | **£5,440/year** |
| **Total Azure annual cost (all environments)** | | **~£16,320/year** |

*Scale-out to P2v3 for production peak load: +£4,800/year. Redis scale-out to C2: +£3,600/year.*

### 4.2 Legacy Infrastructure Savings

The current system runs on an on-premises IIS Windows Server. Decommissioning this server after Phase 6 eliminates:

- Windows Server licence renewal
- Hardware maintenance contract
- On-premises IT operational overhead (patching, monitoring, incident response)

Indicative annual saving from decommission: **£8,000–£15,000/year** depending on whether the server is dedicated or shared.

### 4.3 Reduced Maintenance Cost

The legacy codebase has zero automated tests, .NET Framework 4.0 (out of mainstream support), and Crystal Reports 13 (GAC-only, incompatible with current platforms). Every change carries high regression risk and requires a Windows developer environment to build.

Post-migration, the .NET 10 modular monolith with 70+ automated tests and a CI pipeline substantially reduces the cost and risk of each future change:

| Maintenance scenario | Legacy cost (est.) | Post-migration cost (est.) | Annual saving |
|---|---|---|---|
| Security patch applied | 2 days developer + 1 day test | 1 day developer (CI validates) | 1 day/patch × £800 |
| Bug fix (simple) | 1.5 days (no tests; manual regression) | 0.5 days (tests provide confidence) | 1 day × £800 |
| Feature addition (small) | 3–5 days (no tests; manual regression across 64 pages) | 1.5–2 days (tests + CI) | 2 days × £800 |
| Emergency hotfix | 1 day + 4-hour manual test cycle | 1 day + 15-minute CI run | 0.5 day × £800 |

**Estimated annual maintenance cost saving:** 15–25 days × £800 = **£12,000–£20,000/year**

| **Net cash flow** | **−£481,070** | **+£17,580** | **+£17,580** | **−£445,910** |

### 5.2 Breakeven Analysis

At a net annual saving of **£37,500/year** (legacy saving + maintenance saving + security saving), the migration investment of ~£500,000 breaks even in approximately **Year 14**.

This is a typical breakeven profile for a legacy migration programme where the primary drivers are **risk reduction and platform sustainability**, not near-term cost saving. The financial case is strengthened by:

1. **Avoided critical incident cost:** A single security incident on the legacy platform (plaintext SQL credential exposure, unpatched .NET 4.0 CVE) could cost £100,000–£500,000 in regulatory, reputational, and remediation costs. The migration eliminates this risk class entirely.

2. **Avoided cost of forced migration:** As .NET Framework 4.0 becomes further unsupported and Windows Server versions used for IIS hosting approach end-of-life, the cost of a forced emergency migration (without planning, documentation, or test coverage) would substantially exceed the cost of this planned programme.

3. **Enabling future capability:** The .NET 10 modular monolith enables future enhancements (API integrations, mobile access, cloud-native scaling) that are structurally impossible on the current WebForms stack. The value of these future capabilities is not quantified in this model but is available to the executive sponsor as a strategic upside.

### 5.3 AI Productivity Uplift Sensitivity

| Scenario | AI uplift assumption | Migration cost | Breakeven |
|---|---|---|---|
| High (AI fully realised) | 42% | £410,000 | ~Year 11 |
| Medium (AI partially realised) | 25% | £480,000 | ~Year 13 |
| Low (AI minimal) | 10% | £530,000 | ~Year 14 |
| No AI | 0% | £580,000 | ~Year 16 |

The AI augmentation investment (£2,400 one-time + £3,600/year) pays back within the first month of the programme through accelerated delivery of the Phase 0 documentation and test suite alone.
